title: JavaScript: Deep Flatten Array
statement: Implement a function flatten(arr) that recursively flattens an array of arbitrarily nested arrays into a single 1-dimensional array.
description: Implement a function flatten(arr) that recursively flattens an array of arbitrarily nested arrays into a single 1-dimensional array.

title: JavaScript: Promisify Node Callback
statement: Implement a `promisify(fn)` function that takes a standard Node.js error-first callback function `(arg1, ..., callback)` and returns a function returning a Promise.
description: Implement a `promisify(fn)` function that takes a standard Node.js error-first callback function `(arg1, ..., callback)` and returns a function returning a Promise.

title: Reverse a String
statement: Reverse the provided string and return the reversed string. For example, 'hello' should become 'olleh'.
description: Reverse the provided string and return the reversed string. For example, 'hello' should become 'olleh'.

title: Diff Two Arrays (Symmetric Difference)
statement: Compare two arrays and return a new array with any items only found in one of the two given arrays, but not both. In other words, return the symmetric difference of the two arrays.
description: Compare two arrays and return a new array with any items only found in one of the two given arrays, but not both. In other words, return the symmetric difference of the two arrays.

title: TypeScript: Implement Concat<T, U>
statement: Implement the JavaScript `Array.concat` function in the TypeScript type system. A type takes two tuple arguments and returns a new tuple including inputs in left-to-right order.
description: Implement the JavaScript `Array.concat` function in the TypeScript type system. A type takes two tuple arguments and returns a new tuple including inputs in left-to-right order.
starterCode: type Concat<T extends readonly any[], U extends readonly any[]> = any;

typescript.starterCode: type Concat<T extends readonly any[], U extends readonly any[]> = any;

title: JavaScript: Function Currying
statement: Implement a `curry` function that transforms a function of multiple arguments into a sequence of functions, each taking arguments until all required arguments are provided.
description: Implement a `curry` function that transforms a function of multiple arguments into a sequence of functions, each taking arguments until all required arguments are provided.

title: JavaScript: Deep Clone Object
statement: Implement a function deepClone(value) that creates a deep copy of an object or array. Modifying the cloned copy should never mutate the original object.
description: Implement a function deepClone(value) that creates a deep copy of an object or array. Modifying the cloned copy should never mutate the original object.

title: JavaScript: Memoize Function
statement: Write a function memoize(fn) that returns a memoized version of fn. Subsequent calls with identical arguments should return the cached result without re-executing fn.
description: Write a function memoize(fn) that returns a memoized version of fn. Subsequent calls with identical arguments should return the cached result without re-executing fn.
sampleTests: const fn = memoize((x) => x * 2); fn(4); fn(4); // computed once

javascript.example: const fn = memoize((x) => x * 2); fn(4); fn(4); // computed once

title: Chunky Monkey (Array Chunks)
statement: Write a function that splits an array (first argument) into groups the length of size (second argument) and returns them as a two-dimensional array.
description: Write a function that splits an array (first argument) into groups the length of size (second argument) and returns them as a two-dimensional array.

title: Factorialize a Number
statement: Return the factorial of the provided integer. If the integer is represented with the letter n, a factorial is the product of all positive integers less than or equal to n. 0! is 1.
description: Return the factorial of the provided integer. If the integer is represented with the letter n, a factorial is the product of all positive integers less than or equal to n. 0! is 1.
